messages:
alice (infra): FYI rolling a change to the structured-log pipeline to handle per-request consent flags at the edge proxy. need quick alignment on sampling + redaction rules before canary deploy.
ben (eng-ml): quick question — do we propagate consent downstream as a field or only keep it at the proxy for routing? cost implications either way.
carla (privacy): we should persist consent_status as a small enum (opt_in / opt_out / unknown) on the log envelope. do NOT keep raw user identifiers in the same event after redaction. auditability needs the consent flag but not PII.
dan (eng-platform): suggested approach: proxy attaches consent_status header, pipeline stores consent_status in metadata; redactor strips user_id/session_id unless consent_status==opt_in. also add sampling heuristics for user_id to control egress volume. example config: ```json
{
  "retain_fields": ["consent_status","region","route"],
  "redact_rules": [
    {"field":"user_id","when_not":"consent_status:opt_in"},
    {"field":"email","always_redact":true}
  ],
  "sampling": {
    "default_rate": 0.05,
    "by_field": {"user_id": 0.01, "error": 1.0},
    "preserve_if": ["consent_status:opt_in","route:replay"]
  }
}
```
eva (sre): want to call out metric/alert impact: if we sample away user_id events we'll lose cardinality for some SLO dashboards; recommend adding an unsampled counter metric (aggregated) and a sampled detail stream.
ben (eng-ml): +1. For model telemetry we need surrogate keys sometimes. Can we hash user_id with salted key and only keep hashed_id for opt_in? hashed id still PII risk per privacy review though.
carla (privacy): hashed ids are allowed only when salt is managed by customer KMS and hashes are one-way. default: no hashed user id in hosted logs. we can allow hashed_id in Dedicated/Private with config toggle.
alice (infra): cost question — what's the expected token/event reduction from these rules? dan, do you have an estimate for pipeline bytes delta?
dan (eng-platform): rough numbers from staging: removing user_id/email from 100k events -> ~12% payload decrease; sampling default 5% -> gross event drop ~88%. overall storage cost down ~70% for that workload.
ben (eng-ml): Important for model evals: keep a small deterministic sample (e.g., 0.1%) with full payload for quality checks. Make that sample flagged via "preserve_if": ["consent_status:opt_in","model_eval_candidate:true"].
deploy-bot: deploy started: structured-log-redactor v2 -> canary cluster (canary=cluster-3). expected drain 60s, watch logs.canary.redactor.errors.
eva (sre): alert tuning note: adjust the "redactor_error_rate" alert to 0.5% for canary window; if >1% trigger pager. also add Grafana panel for "sampled_event_rate" and "unsampled_counter" to detect regressions.
carla (privacy): edge case: aggregated metrics that include user counts must be computed server-side from unsampled counters, not reconstructed from sampled traces. add doc note in schema.
alice (infra): ok action items: (1) dan to push updated redaction config + canary (2) ben to request a deterministic eval sample rule (3) carla to add privacy constraints for hashed ids (4) eva to update alerts/dashboards. plan to roll to 30% after 24h canary if redactor_error_rate < 0.5%.
dan (eng-platform): on it, will post PR with the manifest and canary DAG.
ben (eng-ml): i'll add model_eval_candidate tagging in our ingestion rules today. :eyes:
carla (privacy): will add hashed-id policy to privacy playbook and send clip for legal review.
eva (sre): i'll create Grafana dashboard patch and a short Runbook snippet for debugging redactor failures.
alice (infra): thanks team. if you hit policy blockers ping me. otherwise aim for canary watch by EOD.
